## 開篇固定收益論點

8月5日美國固定收益市場收盤時，連續兩個交易日的存續期間漲勢暫歇，但能源降溫帶動通膨趨緩的邏輯並未逆轉。2年期美國公債殖利率下跌2個基點至4.18%，5年期與10年期分別持平於4.33%及4.63%，30年期則下跌1個基點至5.17%。2s10s曲線因而陡峭2個基點至45個基點，2s30s陡峭1個基點至99個基點。前端仍有溫和買盤支撐，但在伊朗與阿曼從談判推進至就荷姆茲海峽航運路線達成協議後，曲線腹部與長端續漲空間已相當有限。

最值得注意的是持平的10年期名目殖利率內部變化：10年期實質殖利率上升1個基點至2.41%，損益兩平通膨率則下降1個基點至2.22%。近期能源通膨風險持續消退，但國內政策仍具限制性，投資人持有存續期間所要求的實質報酬也未下降。7月服務業活動穩定擴張，企業新增就業低於預期，投入成本仍居高不下。Neel Kashkari主張應從現在開始逐步升息；Lisa Cook則表示，若通膨未能恢復降溫，她已準備採取行動。油價下跌降低了外部通膨的尾端風險，卻未解決Fed面對的國內通膨僵固難題。

美國財政部透過債務管理，避免政策張力觸發長端新一波賣壓。官員決定至少未來數季維持名目付息債券與浮動利率票據規模不變，任何調整都將延至2027年較晚時候；下週$1,250億再融資預計籌得約$287億新資金。不過，這僅是戰術性利多。本季借款額已上調至$7,390億，而且財政部將未來可能增加付息債券發行的措辭由「增加」改為「調整」，在對國庫券依賴升高之際保留更多彈性。近期存續期間供給穩定，壓住殖利率，卻未消除5.17%長債殖利率所反映的財政溢價。

信用與跨資產表現顯示，市場流動性依然充足，但市場已未延續前一日的全面利多行情。投資級與高收益債基金近乎持平；與此同時，新交易既顯示私募市場擁有可觀承接能力，也反映投資人對槓桿、資金用途及債權人保障的條件日益嚴格。美股在連漲四天後回落，半導體指數下跌1.40%，美元指數下跌0.24%。儘管名目美國公債持平，黃金期貨仍大漲6.09%至$4,345。整體訊號並非成長或融資衝擊再現，而是市場進入暫歇：能源壓力緩解、Fed偏鷹溝通、財政存續期間風險及政策避險需求仍同時發揮作用。

## 美國公債利率、Fed 定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

殖利率曲線小幅陡峭，源於前端表現較強，而非長端再度走弱。2年期殖利率下跌2個基點，5年期與10年期則持平，使2s10s回升至45個基點，扭轉前一交易日的牛市趨平。30年期殖利率下跌1個基點，令2s30s維持在99個基點，接近Fed會議後所處區域；政策不確定性當時已轉移至較長期的通膨、財政及公信力溢價。單日走勢溫和，但曲線形態顯示，近期能源壓力下降可降低市場對升息急迫性的預期，卻未實質改變投資人持有中長期存續期間所要求的補償。

即使油價帶動債券上漲，中期定價仍偏緊縮。四個代表性付息債券殖利率一週均下跌3至4個基點，但月度變化仍從2年期上升4個基點，一路擴大至5年期上升10個基點、10年期14個基點及30年期19個基點。因此，曲線同時反映兩種判斷：短期通膨衝擊已改善到足以收復7月底部分跌幅，但長端對實質利率與供給負擔的定價仍高於一個月前。單日盤整並未消除這兩種時間尺度的落差。

通膨連結定價進一步凸顯這項差異。10年期損益兩平通膨率降至2.22%，一週跌幅擴大至4個基點；10年期實質殖利率則較一個月前高出15個基點。荷姆茲海峽的進展足夠具體，使通膨補償延續下滑：伊朗表示，已與阿曼就一條擬議航運路線達成協議，美國原油收在每桶約$75。然而，最終公開版本未提及美國參與；另一項可能為期60天的安排，仍須面對胡塞武裝對區域航運的威脅。市場仍認同通膨趨緩方向，但尚未認定實體航運已完全恢復正常。

Fed官員的溝通使實質利率維持堅挺。Kashkari是7月決議維持利率不變時持異議的三位官員之一；他表示央行應開始緩步升息，也不排除年底前升息三次，儘管他對9月是否行動尚未決定。支持維持利率不變的Cook也設下相近的條件門檻：通膨連續五年高於目標，提高價格與薪資設定行為根深蒂固的風險。她同時指出，油價下降、關稅效應消退及AI相關壓力減輕，都可能讓央行避免再次升息。政策分歧日益集中在必須觀察到多少通膨降溫，才能避免等待的代價過高，而非2%目標是否仍具約束力。

先前市場定價仍反映年底前升息一次，低於前一週的兩次。收盤時並未進一步加深這項偏鴿定價，因為國內經濟訊號仍多空交錯。7月服務業活動維持原有增速，成本上升持續壓迫企業，民間部門招聘則弱於預期。招聘疲弱最終可望降低需求壓力，但投入成本僵固，使Fed無法僅憑一項調查便斷定招聘轉弱已開始壓低需求。殖利率曲線反映兩股力量的平衡：眼前升息的急迫性下降，讓2年期殖利率可以小幅回落；但恢復物價穩定最終所需的緊縮程度仍未明朗，使10年期實質殖利率維持在2.4%以上。

再融資公告提供近期確定性，卻未帶來持久的財政解方。財政部決定至少未來數季維持現行付息債券與浮動利率票據規模，並保留未來若增發、仍偏向較短天期的方針，降低長期存續期間供給突然增加的風險。但這也意味國庫券必須承擔更多借款需求；本季借款需求增加$680億至$7,390億。諮詢委員會表示，現行預測可能需要在10月1日開始的會計年度提高付息債券發行量，並敦促採用可保留彈性的措辭。延後發出增量訊號，今日雖可支撐長端，日後轉換時的溝通與市場吸收卻可能更為倉促。

較廣泛的信心指標顯示，不宜將財政溢價視為資金正積極逃離美國資產。5月外國投資人持有$9.4兆美國公債，較一年前增加4%；今年以來，10年期美國公債、美元及美國投資級債券利差同時遭遇賣壓的情況，只出現在約2%的交易日及連續5個交易日區間。不過，邊際壓力依然可見。儘管美國殖利率處於高檔，美元指數仍走弱；估算的30年期期限溢價則升至1.56%，創2013年以來最高。持有結構穩定、市場運作正常，可以與政策不透明度與財政存續期間風險的代價上升同時存在。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

整體信用市場以盤整作收。LQD下跌0.02%、HYG下跌0.04%、JNK下跌0.08%；相較近乎持平的美國公債曲線，總報酬變化不大。更重要的發展是，市場對可明確辨識、能產生現金流的交易仍願意出資，但面對供給集中或債權人地位薄弱時，要求的補償正不斷提高。這項差異延續前一交易日投資級債承接強勁、財務贊助方未能抽回資金的對比，但目前案例已將分析延伸至私募、直接貸款及重整控制權。

AI相關發債仍是公開投資級債投資組合面臨的最大潛在承接挑戰。超大型雲端業者大量供給，已迫使投資人出售存量債券，為新交易騰出資金，Amazon發行$250億債券時便出現這種情況。7月期間，Meta債券利差平均擴大約22個基點，Oracle則擴大29個基點。歐洲信用市場目前因承接的發行量少於美國而受益，但Alphabet大規模首度發行英鎊、瑞士法郎及歐元債券，顯示發債供給正擴散至全球。真正風險並非現金充裕的科技發行人立即出現償債問題，而是投資組合為生產性報酬仍不確定的一再舉債騰出空間時，利差持續承壓。

私募信貸顯示，只要交易經濟效益清楚，大型風險部位仍能獲得資金。Ares正牽頭提供$22億直接貸款，支持MedImpact Holdings計畫收購位於波多黎各的醫療保健公司Medical Card System。該貸款利率可能至少較基準利率高出8個百分點，也是今年稍早創紀錄贖回潮擾亂該產業以來規模最大的交易之一。若能以這項利差順利成交，將證明市場承接能力可觀，但其成本也使收購案的現金流創造能力及再融資路徑成為核心。私募流動性仍然存在，但並不便宜，也不會忽視槓桿。

United Launch Alliance另覓私募管道進行再融資。這家由Boeing與Lockheed Martin合資的火箭公司，正透過U.S. Bancorp、Mizuho及Wells Fargo安排的純私募發行，尋求籌集約$5億。債券不會註冊，也無法在公開市場交易。ULA是美國敏感國防衛星及Amazon等商業客戶的發射服務供應商，讓這筆交易具備明確的策略性收入基礎。該案也說明，為何整體發行數據低估了融資來源的分散程度：即使公開市場投資組合已在消化龐大科技債供給，擁有特殊資產的借款人仍可進入雙邊或機構管道。

Pfleiderer則顯示債權人接管更為嚴厲的一面。其2029年到期票據逾80%的持有人，包括Arini與Silver Point，在去年12月一筆融資未能穩定公司後，同意接管這家木質板材生產商。該筆€1.35億融資由Monarch Alternative Capital出資，並包含股東貸款；公司先將能產生現金流的Silekol移出既有債券持有人的擔保範圍，再以該資產提供擔保。隨著歐洲營建業走弱，公司持續消耗現金。債券持有人目前已再投入約€8,700萬，其中包括€4,700萬初始承諾，同時推動更全面的重整與股權移轉。

事件順序之所以重要，在於它揭示以文件條款彈性取代營運復甦的極限。移轉擔保品可以創造優先順位較高的流動性並延長緩衝期，卻也可能削弱其餘債權人的保障，而且無法改善需求、利潤率或現金消耗。八個月後，失去對最強資產求償權的持有人，如今必須提供救援資金並接掌控制權。這並非歐洲融資普遍失靈，而是警示優先順位上移交易既有利益重分配風險；若基礎企業無法產生足夠現金支撐調整後的資本結構，這類安排能維持的時間也很有限。

因此，各融資管道仍正常運作，但選擇性明顯。公開投資級債投資組合面臨超大型雲端業者供給造成的重新定價；直接貸款機構可以至少800個基點的利差，為$22億收購案提供資金；具策略重要性的航太發行人可尋求私募債再融資；承壓的歐洲債券持有人則在先前流動性措施失敗後接管公司。整體基金價格穩定，與這些更鮮明的個別交易結果並不矛盾。各市場共同檢視的核心是現金流相對融資成本的持久性、資金用途，以及原始計畫落空時貸款人可執行的法律地位。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

全球利率走勢並未指向單一政策方向，但確實強化美國市場所呈現的差異：眼前能源通膨下降，國內約束卻持續存在。中國以境外發行史上最低殖利率吸收長天期主權債供給，印度維持政策利率不變，短端債券上漲，東南亞通膨則放緩，但殘餘壓力各異。這些結果提高部分海外長天期資產的吸引力，也降低同步升息的可能性；然而，匯率防衛、當地財政需求及核心通膨並不一致，因此無法形成對美國公債的全球一致買盤。

中國呈現最鮮明的存續期間對比。財政部分別發行人民幣10億元的15年期與30年期境外債券，殖利率為1.99%及2.24%；2年期、3年期與5年期債券殖利率則分別為1.27%、1.30%及1.43%。長券殖利率創境外發行計畫歷史新低，中國境內10年期公債殖利率週二已降至兩個月低點1.71%。在可比美國殖利率仍居高檔之際需求仍然強勁，顯示全球存續期間風險正依不同的通膨、匯率及供給體制定價，也為國際投資人提供名目殖利率低得多的另一個長天期債券市場。

印度央行按兵不動，帶動較典型的政策路徑行情。印度央行一致決議將附買回政策利率維持在5.25%，並維持中性立場。總裁Sanjay Malhotra未暗示將收回流動性後，5年期政府債殖利率下跌8個基點，10年期則下跌3個基點。市場對10月升息的定價由100%降至65%。印度央行將本會計年度通膨預測由5.1%下調至5%，並將成長預測由6.6%上調至6.7%；儘管6月通膨高於4%目標，且印度約90%原油仰賴進口，央行仍認為基礎壓力受控。

不過，印度央行的判斷仍取決於匯率與食品價格傳導。6月推出的措施吸引逾$400億外幣流入，但盧比仍是亞洲表現較弱的貨幣之一。降雨不足、稻米與豆類播種進度落後，使食品價格仍顯脆弱，消費品公司也正準備新一輪漲價。印度央行認為能源衝擊只是暫時現象，加上流動性仍充裕，使印度短端債券得以上漲。若匯率走弱或傳導更廣，這項政策空間將迅速收窄，尤其1月至3月當季經濟成長已達7.8%。

東南亞數據說明，整體通膨下降在不同經濟體的意義並不相同。菲律賓通膨率由6月的6.4%降至6.2%，低於預期，核心通膨也出現六個月來首次減速。然而，米價仍較一年前上漲17.1%，整體通膨率遠高於央行3%目標，而且今年政策利率已提高50個基點。運輸通膨放緩減輕眼前壓力，披索因而升值0.7%至兌1美元60.75披索；但成長疲弱與食品通膨嚴重並存，政策並無全面轉鴿的空間。

泰國7月CPI由2.42%明顯降至1.95%，月減0.73%，主要由國內燃料價格下降帶動；核心通膨卻由1.23%微升至1.34%。捷克通膨也發出類似的組成警訊：整體通膨率1.7%，仍低於2%目標，但服務業通膨由4.5%加速至4.7%。兩個市場的能源成本下降，均有利存續期間並支持央行耐心觀望；但能源帶來的支撐能否延續，取決於國內通膨組成。即使損益兩平通膨率下降，同樣的差異仍使美國實質殖利率維持堅挺。

日本的日圓防衛，是海外政策與美國公債市場結構之間最直接的連結。FIMA機制允許外國主管機關以美國公債為擔保，隔夜借入美元，每日上限$600億，降低直接出售美國公債的必要。日本財務大臣證實未來可能使用該工具，但沒有官員透露目前是否已動用。估計財務省另持有約$1,620億存款，其中多數存放於外國逆回購池；定期到期的國庫券也可提供美元。這些緩衝降低眼前被迫賣債的風險，但若反覆干預，仍將考驗一項成本高於民間回購市場、原為壓力情境而非日常匯率管理所設計的後盾。

整體海外因素對中期存續期間略為有利，卻不足以推動美國公債全面重新定價。中國長債發行殖利率創低、印度短端上漲，以及亞洲整體通膨放緩，都顯示全球能源衝擊正以不均速度消退。服務業通膨僵固、食品風險及匯率壓力，使各地央行無法同步轉向寬鬆。日本可透過存款、國庫券到期及FIMA限制美國公債出售，但要求擴大該工具的政治訴求，也凸顯潛在干預規模。美國存續期間仍須與走勢分歧的當地曲線競爭，而買方的儲備資產配置決策也愈來愈受政策左右。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

美國收盤時，新興市場債券大致穩定，但個別主權債表現明顯分歧。EMB下跌0.05%，15年以上新興市場美元主權債指數則上漲0.30%。美元指數下跌0.24%，帶來溫和匯率順風，10年期美國公債殖利率則持平。在美元偏弱、10年期美國公債殖利率持平的環境下，當地財政與制度資訊更能區分個別主權風險。加彭與塞內加爾顯示，審計及取得IMF支持的能力，足以主導表現，不受共同全球背景左右；巴西收盤後的決策則表明，即使當地利率極高，也不保證預期已獲錨定。

加彭美元債今年已上漲19.5%，因投資人日益預期該國可在不重整債務的情況下取得IMF方案。其相對美國公債利差已由1月約1,000個基點收窄至約608個基點。塞內加爾則朝相反方向發展：審計發現$70億先前未揭露的借款，與IMF的談判仍停滯，利差因而擴大至1,541個基點。這種對比反映制度面的重新定價，而非單純的大宗商品或美元交易。IMF支持的加彭審計顯示債務較低；塞內加爾的揭露則擴大已確認負債，並迫使該國依賴國內借款履行債務。

加彭趁公信力改善，發行$9.2億、2033年到期的私募債務，但12.65%的發行殖利率仍是今年新興市場主權發行人最高。殖利率其後已降至約11.5%，但仍高於CCC+至CCC-級非洲發行人的10.7%平均值。這筆融資有助處理短期債務並支撐既有債券曲線，然而高成本也顯示，恢復市場准入並不等同債務可持續。2029年與2031年到期債券週三回落，市場歸因於獲利了結；這也使最終審計與IMF協議完成前，不宜採取單向解讀。

巴西央行在美國收盤後採取行動，因此該決策並未驅動已結束的美國公債或新興市場交易時段。決策官員一致將Selic利率下調25個基點至14%，這是連續第四次降息，自3月以來累計寬鬆100個基點。央行未提供前瞻指引，後續週期仍取決於最新數據。7月上旬通膨由4.8%降至4.52%，但央行預測2028年第1季通膨為3.2%，仍高於3%目標，並形容風險異常偏高且上行傾斜。美元走弱有所助益，但財政刺激、聖嬰現象造成的食品風險及Fed偏鷹立場，仍使匯率傳導仍容易受衝擊。

因此，新興市場的分化主要由公信力與融資架構決定，而非共同的美元短缺。加彭在重新評估債務後，取得成本高昂的私募資本及通往IMF支持的路徑；塞內加爾的隱藏借款則破壞同一制度管道。巴西可開始從極度緊縮的利率水準向下調整，卻無法在長期通膨預期仍高於目標時承諾完整寬鬆路徑。硬通貨債基準走勢穩定，掩蓋了這些差異。外匯準備深度、資訊揭露品質、取得多邊機構支持的能力，以及新資金在不同期限上的成本，仍是美元走弱表象下的決定性變數。

## 跨資產

跨資產表現不支持前一日通膨降溫行情單純延續。WTI在先前大跌後僅上漲0.20%至$75.62，Brent上漲0.76%至$79.96，顯示能源衝擊仍受控制，並未重啟。美元指數下跌0.24%至99.654，黃金期貨卻大漲6.09%至$4,345。黃金漲幅過大，無法僅歸因於長期美國公債殖利率下降1個基點或美元溫和走弱，而是反映市場仍需要防範地緣政治協議的執行風險、Fed公信力不確定性，以及美國匯率政策與儲備資產政策互動方式的變化。

股市反映漲勢疲乏，而非普遍避險。S&P 500下跌0.17%、Nasdaq 100下跌0.83%、半導體類股下跌1.40%；此前S&P 500連漲四天，市值增加約$3.7兆。VIX卻下跌4.18%至15.81。這項組合顯示獲利了結與集中度風險，而非系統性壓力突然上升。SpaceX在$1,010億股份解禁前下跌14%，AI領漲態勢也選擇性轉弱。股市暫歇之所以攸關固定收益，是因同一批資本密集型科技企業正創造龐大債券供給；但波動率低檔收盤，並不支持跨市場被迫去槓桿的判斷。

信用基金補足了這幅克制的市場圖像。儘管股市回落、黃金漲勢異常強勁，LQD、HYG、JNK及EMB的波動均低於0.1%。因此，投資人重新評估通膨舒緩、政策不確定性及科技股集中度之際，整體融資條件仍然穩健。黃金則是明顯的矛盾訊號：債券與波動率未顯示急迫壓力，無收益避險資產的需求卻加速上升。固定收益收盤最適合解讀為市場在政策環境尚未明朗之際仍穩定運作，而不是投資人相信能源、財政與Fed風險已經消失。

## 前瞻市場意義

週五官方就業報告必須釐清，民間部門招聘轉弱與7月服務業成本訊號仍居高檔之間，何者才是主導力量。若勞動需求明顯降溫且實質殖利率下降，即使投入價格仍具僵固性，也會強化年底前升息一次已足夠的論點。若招聘仍具韌性，或證據顯示薪資敏感型壓力持續，將印證Kashkari主張開始緊縮，以及Cook對價格設定行為根深蒂固的疑慮。市場將先反映在2年期與5年期區段，但10年期實質殖利率若上升，影響更為重大，因為這代表國內通膨僵固再次壓過能源價格下降帶來的舒緩。

伊朗與阿曼的航運安排，現在需要實體與商業層面的落實。荷姆茲海峽航行持續、安全威脅減少、保險恢復正常，且胡塞武裝未再擾亂航運，才能讓原油及損益兩平通膨率守住近期跌幅。這項結果將降低外部通膨迫使Fed維持緊縮的理由，也有利匯率與食品體系仍顯脆弱的能源進口國。若協議停滯、關鍵參與方遭排除，或船舶再受威脅並推升WTI與Brent突破協議後區間，通膨補償將迅速回升。若實質殖利率同時上升，對債市更為不利，因為能源衝擊與政策公信力溢價都將重現。

下週$1,250億再融資標售，將決定穩定的發行指引能否轉化為實際長期存續期間承接。投標倍數、標售結果相對發行前交易水準的表現，以及投資人配售，將揭示在30年期殖利率高於5%、估算期限溢價達1.56%之際，市場是否願意接受現行規模。若結果有序，即使國庫券需承擔更多本季$7,390億借款需求，近期供給問題仍可延後。若需求疲弱，財政部將未來措辭由「增加」改為「調整」所帶來的安定作用將減弱，並在官員正式改變標售規模前，提前讓最終2027年付息債券轉換風險反映於10年至30年期殖利率曲線。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 5 U.S. fixed-income close paused the two-session duration rally without reversing its energy-disinflation logic. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.18%, the 5- and 10-year yields were unchanged at 4.33% and 4.63%, and the 30-year eased 1 basis point to 5.17%. That left the 2s10s curve 2 basis points steeper at 45 and 2s30s 1 basis point steeper at 99. The front end retained modest relief, but the belly and long end found little room to extend after Iran and Oman moved from negotiations toward an agreed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.

The most revealing change was inside the unchanged 10-year nominal yield. The 10-year real yield rose 1 basis point to 2.41% as the breakeven fell 1 basis point to 2.22%. Immediate energy inflation risk continued to recede, yet domestic policy restraint and the required real return on duration did not. Services activity expanded steadily in July, companies added fewer jobs than expected, and input costs remained elevated. Neel Kashkari called for incremental increases to begin now, while Lisa Cook said she was prepared to act if disinflation failed to resume. Lower oil narrowed the external inflation tail; it did not resolve the Fed's domestic persistence problem.

Treasury debt management prevented that policy tension from becoming a fresh long-end selloff. Officials kept nominal coupon and floating-rate note sizes steady for at least several quarters, pushing any adjustment well into 2027, and next week's $125 billion refunding is expected to raise about $28.7 billion of new cash. The relief is tactical. Current-quarter borrowing was raised to $739 billion, and Treasury changed its description of potential future coupon sales from "increases" to "changes," preserving more flexibility as bill reliance grows. Stable near-term duration supply contained yields, but it did not remove the fiscal premium embedded in a 5.17% long bond.

Credit and cross assets describe a market that remained liquid but was no longer extending the previous day's broad relief. Investment-grade and high-yield funds were almost unchanged, even as new transactions showed both substantial private-market capacity and increasingly strict terms around leverage, use of proceeds and creditor protection. U.S. equities slipped after a four-day surge, the semiconductor index fell 1.40%, and the Dollar Index declined 0.24%. Gold futures rose 6.09% to $4,345 despite flat nominal Treasuries. The combined signal is not a renewed growth or funding shock; it is a pause in which energy relief, hawkish Fed communication, fiscal duration risk and demand for policy hedges remained simultaneously active.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The curve's small steepening came from front-end outperformance rather than renewed long-end weakness. A 2-basis-point decline in the 2-year against unchanged 5- and 10-year yields moved 2s10s back to 45 basis points, reversing the prior session's bull flattening. The 30-year's 1-basis-point decline kept 2s30s at 99, close to the post-Fed region where policy uncertainty had migrated into longer inflation, fiscal and credibility premiums. The daily move was mild, but its shape says that reduced near-term energy pressure can lower the expected urgency of tightening without materially changing the compensation demanded for intermediate and long duration.

The horizon remains restrictive even after the oil-led rally. All four representative coupon yields were 3 to 4 basis points lower over 1 week, but the monthly change still ranged from a 4-basis-point rise at 2 years to increases of 10 basis points at 5 years, 14 at 10 years and 19 at 30 years. The curve therefore carries two different judgments. The near-term inflation impulse has improved enough to retrace part of the late-July selloff, while the long end still prices a larger real-rate and supply burden than it did a month earlier. One flat session did not reconcile those horizons.

Inflation-linked pricing sharpened that distinction. The 10-year breakeven fell to 2.22%, extending its weekly decline to 4 basis points, while the 10-year real yield held 15 basis points above its month-earlier level. The Hormuz development was concrete enough to preserve the decline in inflation compensation: Iran said it had reached an agreement with Oman on a proposed shipping route, and U.S. oil settled near $75. Yet the final public description did not include a U.S. role, and a separate prospective 60-day arrangement still faced Houthi threats to regional shipping. The market retained the disinflation direction without treating physical normalization as complete.

Fed communication kept the real-rate component firm. Kashkari, one of the three officials who dissented from the July hold, said the central bank should begin raising rates slowly and did not rule out three increases before year-end, though he remained undecided about September. Cook, who supported the hold, set a similar conditional boundary: five years of above-target inflation increased the risk that price and wage setting would become entrenched. She also identified lower oil, fading tariff effects and less AI-related pressure as routes that could avoid another increase. The policy split is increasingly about how much disinflation must be observed before delay becomes costly, not about whether the 2% objective remains binding.

Earlier market pricing still embedded one increase by year-end, down from two the prior week. The close did not extend that dovish adjustment because the domestic activity mix remained ambiguous. July services activity held its pace, rising costs continued to weigh on firms, and private hiring was softer than expected. Weak hiring can eventually reduce demand pressure, but persistent input costs leave the Fed unable to infer that channel from one survey. The resulting equilibrium is visible in the curve: the 2-year can edge lower as an immediate hike becomes less urgent, while the 10-year real yield remains above 2.4% because the eventual restraint needed to restore price stability is unsettled.

The refunding announcement supplied near-term certainty without a durable fiscal resolution. Treasury maintained current coupon and floating-rate note sizes for at least several quarters and retained a bias toward shorter maturities for any future increases. That reduces the risk of an immediate long-duration supply surprise. It also means bills must carry more of a borrowing requirement that rose by $68 billion to $739 billion for the quarter. The advisory committee said current projections could warrant higher coupon issuance in the fiscal year beginning October 1 and urged language that preserves flexibility. Delaying the signal supports today's long end, but it increases the risk that the eventual transition must be communicated and absorbed more abruptly.

Broader confidence measures argue against treating the fiscal premium as an active flight from U.S. assets. Foreign investors held $9.4 trillion of Treasuries in May, 4% more than a year earlier, and simultaneous selloffs in 10-year Treasuries, the dollar and U.S. investment-grade spreads have occurred on only about 2% of trading days and rolling five-day periods this year. The pressure is nevertheless visible at the margin. The Dollar Index has weakened despite elevated U.S. yields, and the estimated 30-year term premium reached 1.56%, its highest since 2013. Stable ownership and functioning markets can coexist with a rising price for policy opacity and fiscal duration.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit finished in a holding pattern. LQD slipped 0.02%, HYG fell 0.04% and JNK declined 0.08%, small total-return moves beside the near-flat Treasury curve. The more important development was a widening divide between capital that remained available for identifiable cash-generating transactions and capital that demanded compensation for supply concentration or weak creditor position. That distinction extends the prior session's contrast between strong investment-grade absorption and failed sponsor extraction, but the current cases move the analysis into private placements, direct lending and restructuring control.

AI-related issuance remains the largest prospective absorption challenge for public investment-grade portfolios. Heavy hyperscaler supply has already required investors to sell outstanding bonds to fund new deals, as occurred around Amazon's $25 billion offering. During July, Meta bond spreads widened by about 22 basis points on average and Oracle's by 29 basis points. European credit has so far benefited from carrying less of that issuance than the U.S. market, but Alphabet's large sterling, Swiss-franc and euro debuts show that the supply is becoming more global. The relevant risk is not immediate solvency at cash-rich technology issuers; it is persistent spread pressure as portfolios create room for repeated borrowing whose productive return remains uncertain.

Private credit demonstrated that large risk can still clear when the economics are explicit. Ares is leading a $2.2 billion direct loan supporting MedImpact Holdings' planned acquisition of Puerto Rico-based healthcare company Medical Card System. The facility could pay at least 8 percentage points over the benchmark rate and is one of the largest transactions since record redemptions disrupted the sector earlier in the year. Completion at that margin would show substantial capacity, but at a cost that makes the acquisition's cash generation and refinancing path central. Private liquidity is available; it is not inexpensive or indifferent to leverage.

United Launch Alliance found another private route for refinancing. The Boeing and Lockheed Martin rocket venture is seeking about $500 million through a true private placement arranged by U.S. Bancorp, Mizuho and Wells Fargo. The bonds would be unregistered and unavailable in public markets. ULA's position as a launch provider for sensitive U.S. defense satellites and commercial customers including Amazon gives the transaction a specific strategic revenue base. The deal also illustrates why aggregate issuance figures understate financing dispersion: borrowers with specialized assets can access bilateral or institutional channels even when public portfolios are already managing heavy technology supply.

Pfleiderer marks the harsher edge of creditor control. Holders of more than 80% of its notes due 2029, including Arini and Silver Point, agreed to take over the wood-panel producer after a December financing failed to stabilize it. That €135 million package, funded by Monarch Alternative Capital and a shareholder loan, was secured on Silekol after the cash-generative unit was moved away from existing bondholders. The company continued to burn cash as European construction weakened. Bondholders have now supplied about €87 million more, including €47 million of initial commitments, while pursuing a broader restructuring and equity transfer.

The sequence matters because it shows the limit of documentation flexibility as a substitute for operating recovery. Moving collateral can create senior liquidity and extend runway, but it can also weaken the remaining creditor pool without fixing demand, margins or cash burn. Eight months later, the holders that lost access to the strongest asset are providing rescue funding and assuming control. This is not a generalized European funding failure. It is a warning that priming transactions carry both redistribution risk and a short shelf life when the underlying business cannot generate enough cash to support the revised capital structure.

Credit conditions are therefore functional but selective across every channel. Public investment-grade portfolios face supply-induced repricing from hyperscalers; direct lenders can fund a $2.2 billion acquisition at a spread of at least 800 basis points; a strategically important aerospace issuer can seek private bond refinancing; and stressed European bondholders can take control after an earlier liquidity maneuver failed. Stable broad fund prices are compatible with these sharper transaction-level outcomes. The common discipline is the durability of cash flow relative to financing cost, the use of proceeds and the lender's enforceable position when the original plan disappoints.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Global rates offered no single policy direction, but they did reinforce the U.S. distinction between lower immediate energy inflation and persistent domestic constraints. China absorbed long sovereign duration at record-low offshore yields, India held policy while its short end rallied, and Southeast Asian inflation slowed with very different residual pressures. These outcomes improve selected foreign-duration alternatives and reduce the case for synchronized tightening. They do not create a uniform global bid for Treasuries because currency defense, local fiscal needs and core inflation remain uneven.

China supplied the cleanest duration contrast. The Ministry of Finance sold CNY1 billion each of 15-year and 30-year offshore bonds at 1.99% and 2.24%, alongside 2-, 3- and 5-year notes at 1.27%, 1.30% and 1.43%. The long yields were record lows for the offshore program, and the onshore 10-year had already fallen to a two-month low of 1.71% on Tuesday. Strong demand while comparable U.S. yields remain elevated shows that global duration risk is being priced through distinct inflation, currency and supply regimes. It also gives international investors an alternative long-duration market at a much lower nominal yield.

India's hold produced a more conventional policy-path rally. The RBI unanimously kept the repo rate at 5.25% and maintained a neutral stance. Five-year government yields fell 8 basis points, compared with 3 basis points at 10 years, after Governor Sanjay Malhotra avoided signaling liquidity absorption. Pricing for an October increase dropped to 65% from 100%. The RBI lowered its fiscal-year inflation forecast to 5% from 5.1% and raised growth to 6.7% from 6.6%, arguing that underlying pressure remained contained despite June inflation exceeding its 4% target and India importing roughly 90% of its crude.

That confidence remains conditional on currency and food transmission. Measures introduced in June attracted more than $40 billion of foreign-currency inflows, yet the rupee remained among Asia's weaker performers. Deficient rainfall and lagging planting of rice and pulses leave food vulnerable, while consumer companies are preparing another round of price increases. India's curve can rally at the short end because the central bank sees the energy shock as temporary and liquidity remains ample. A weak currency or broader pass-through would close that policy space quickly, especially after growth reached 7.8% in the January-March quarter.

Southeast Asian releases showed why lower headline inflation does not mean the same thing across economies. Philippine inflation slowed to 6.2% from June's 6.4%, below expectations, and core inflation decelerated for the first time in six months. Rice prices still rose 17.1% from a year earlier, the headline rate remained far above the central bank's 3% target, and policy had already been raised 50 basis points this year. The peso gained 0.7% to 60.75 per dollar as slower transport inflation eased the immediate pressure, but weak growth and severe food inflation leave little room for a broad dovish interpretation.

Thailand's July CPI slowed more decisively to 1.95% from 2.42%, with a 0.73% monthly decline driven mainly by cheaper domestic fuel. Core inflation, however, edged up to 1.34% from 1.23%. Czech inflation offered a similar composition warning: the 1.7% headline rate stayed below the 2% target, while services inflation accelerated to 4.7% from 4.5%. Across both markets, lower energy costs support duration and policy patience, but the domestic component determines whether that relief persists. The same distinction is keeping U.S. real yields firm even as breakevens compress.

Japan's yen defense remains the largest direct link between foreign policy and Treasury market structure. The FIMA facility permits a foreign authority to borrow dollars overnight against Treasuries up to a $60 billion daily limit, reducing the need for outright sales. Japan's finance minister confirmed that the facility could be used in future, although no official disclosed current usage. The Ministry of Finance is also estimated to hold about $162 billion in deposits, much of it in the foreign reverse-repo pool, and regular bill maturities can provide dollars. Those buffers reduce immediate forced-sale risk; repeated intervention would still test a backstop priced above private repo and designed for stress rather than routine currency management.

The net foreign impulse is mildly supportive to intermediate duration but not to a wholesale Treasury rerating. China's record-low long issuance, India's front-end rally and softer Asian headline inflation all show that the global energy shock is fading unevenly. Sticky services, food risk and currency pressure keep local central banks from converging on easy policy. Japan can limit Treasury sales through deposits, bill maturities and FIMA, yet the political request to expand that facility highlights the potential scale of intervention. U.S. duration still competes with divergent local curves and a buyer base whose reserve decisions are increasingly policy-dependent.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt was stable at the U.S. close even as sovereign-specific outcomes diverged sharply. EMB slipped 0.05%, while the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign bond index gained 0.30%. The Dollar Index fell 0.24%, providing a modest currency tailwind, and the 10-year Treasury yield was unchanged. That combination leaves local fiscal and institutional information as the more powerful separator. Gabon and Senegal now demonstrate how audits and IMF access can overwhelm a common global backdrop, while Brazil's post-close decision shows that even very high local rates do not guarantee anchored expectations.

Gabon has returned 19.5% in dollar bonds this year as investors increasingly expect an IMF program without restructuring. Its spread has narrowed to about 608 basis points over Treasuries from roughly 1,000 in January. Senegal moved in the opposite direction to 1,541 basis points after an audit identified $7 billion of previously hidden borrowing and IMF talks remained stalled. The contrast is an institutional repricing rather than a simple commodity or dollar trade. Gabon's IMF-supported audit indicated lower debt, while Senegal's disclosure expanded the recognized liability and left the country relying on domestic borrowing to meet obligations.

Gabon converted that improvement into $920 million of private-placement debt maturing in 2033, but the 12.65% issue yield was the highest for an emerging sovereign this year. It has since fallen to about 11.5%, still above the 10.7% average for African issuers in the CCC+ to CCC- range. The financing helps address short-term obligations and supports the existing curve, yet the cost shows that restored access is not the same as debt sustainability. Wednesday's pullback in the 2029 and 2031 bonds, attributed to profit-taking, also limits a one-way reading before the final audit and an IMF agreement are complete.

Brazil's central bank moved after the U.S. close, so the decision did not drive the completed Treasury or EM session. Policymakers unanimously cut the Selic by 25 basis points to 14%, the fourth consecutive reduction and 100 basis points of cumulative easing since March. They offered no forward guidance and kept the cycle dependent on incoming data. Early-July inflation slowed to 4.52% from 4.8%, but the bank projected 3.2% inflation for Q1 2028 against a 3% target and described risks as unusually high with an upward skew. A weaker dollar helps, though fiscal stimulus, El Nino food risk and a hawkish Fed keep the currency channel exposed.

The EM distribution is consequently governed by credibility and financing architecture more than by a common dollar shortage. Gabon obtained expensive private capital and a path toward IMF support after a favorable debt reassessment. Senegal's hidden borrowing impaired the same institutional channel. Brazil can begin calibrating down from an exceptionally restrictive rate, but it cannot commit to a full easing path while long-run expectations remain above target. Stable hard-currency benchmarks mask these differences. Reserve depth, disclosure quality, multilateral access and the maturity cost of new money remain the decisive variables beneath a softer dollar.

## Cross asset

Cross assets reject a simple extension of the prior day's disinflation rally. WTI rose only 0.20% to $75.62 and Brent gained 0.76% to $79.96 after their sharp earlier declines, leaving the energy shock contained rather than renewed. The Dollar Index fell 0.24% to 99.654, but gold futures surged 6.09% to $4,345. Gold's move was too large to attribute only to the 1-basis-point decline in long Treasuries or a modestly weaker dollar. It points to persistent demand for protection against geopolitical execution risk, Fed credibility uncertainty and the changing interaction between U.S. currency and reserve policy.

Equities showed exhaustion rather than broad risk aversion. The S&P 500 slipped 0.17%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.83% and semiconductors lost 1.40% after a four-day S&P 500 advance worth about $3.7 trillion. The VIX nevertheless declined 4.18% to 15.81. That pairing indicates profit-taking and concentration risk, not a sudden rise in systemwide stress. SpaceX fell 14% before a $101 billion share unlock, and AI leadership weakened selectively. The equity pause matters for fixed income because the same capital-intensive technology complex is creating heavy bond supply, but the low volatility close argues against forced cross-market deleveraging.

Credit funds completed the restrained picture. LQD, HYG, JNK and EMB all moved by less than 0.1%, despite the equity pullback and extraordinary gold rally. Broad financing conditions therefore remained intact as investors reassessed the mix of inflation relief, policy uncertainty and technology concentration. The independent contradiction is gold: bonds and volatility did not signal acute stress, yet demand for a non-yielding hedge accelerated. The fixed-income close is best read as stable market function around an unresolved policy regime, not as confidence that the energy, fiscal and Fed risks have disappeared.

## Forward Market Significance

Friday's government employment report must separate softer private hiring from the still-elevated cost signals in July services. A material cooling in labor demand accompanied by lower real yields would strengthen the case that one year-end increase is sufficient even if input prices remain sticky. Resilient hiring or evidence that wage-sensitive pressure is persisting would validate Kashkari's call to begin tightening and Cook's concern about entrenched price setting. The first response should appear in the 2- and 5-year sectors, but a rise in 10-year real yields would be more consequential because it would show that domestic persistence is again overwhelming the relief supplied by lower energy prices.

The Iran-Oman shipping arrangement now needs physical and commercial execution. Sustained passage through Hormuz, fewer security threats, normalized insurance and no renewed Houthi disruption would allow crude and breakevens to retain their recent declines. That outcome would reduce the externally generated case for Fed restraint while helping energy importers whose currencies and food systems remain vulnerable. A stalled agreement, exclusion of key parties or renewed threat to vessels that pushes WTI and Brent back above their post-deal range would restore inflation compensation quickly. A simultaneous rise in real yields would be more damaging because it would revive both the energy shock and the policy-credibility premium.

Next week's $125 billion refunding auctions determine whether stable issuance guidance can translate into actual long-duration absorption. Bid-to-cover, the relationship to supplied when-issued levels and investor allocation will reveal whether the market accepts current sizes with the 30-year yield above 5% and a 1.56% estimated term premium. Orderly results would keep the near-term supply question deferred even as bills absorb more of the $739 billion quarterly borrowing need. Weak demand would make Treasury's shift from future "increases" to "changes" less reassuring and would bring the eventual 2027 coupon transition back into the 10- to 30-year curve before officials formally alter auction sizes.
